answer: Delayed ripple assignment. Each identity slot is assigned by a verifiable random function over a public beacon that emits after registration closes. A horizon of future beacon outputs, unrevealed, fixes slot placement, so an attacker cannot grind addresses toward favorable assignment without a cipher breaking collision resistance of the commitment. Since outcomes are unforeseeable, mass registrations yield no positional edge. An attacker must pay full registration work per independent address, then lose any that collide on later beacons, raising marginal cost per retained identity.
